column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline rule tuning for the livechat targets.
# Format (tab-separated): <ruleId>
#   threshold: IGNORE | WARN | FAIL   (default: FAIL for HIGH/MEDIUM, WARN for LOW)
# Consumed by .github/workflows/zap.yml (rules_file_name). Every override below
# is a deliberate, documented decision — start strict, relax only with a reason.
# See docs/security/zap.md for how to run the scan and why each line exists.
# Suppressions (IGNORE) — findings that are false positives or by-design here.
# 10015 — Incomplete or No Cache-control Header.
# The API deliberately does not send Cache-Control on JSON responses; they are
# not cacheable by default and carry per-request auth. The static hosts DO set
# explicit Cache-Control (ui/nginx.conf, widget/nginx.conf). Noise on the API.

column3: API JSON is non-cacheable by default; static hosts set Cache-Control explicitly

column1: # 10096 — Timestamp Disclosure.
# ZAP flags any integer that looks like a Unix timestamp. Our JSON carries
# `created_at` / `expires_at` ISO fields and numeric ids by design; none are
# secrets. Pure false positive.

column3: Timestamps (created_at/expires_at) are intended API data, not a leak

column1: # 10027 — Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments.
# Fires on words like "TODO"/"query" inside the minified widget/console bundles.
# No secrets are shipped in client code (enforced by trufflehog + no-secrets).

column3: Suspicious-comment heuristic hits minified bundles; no secrets in client JS

column1: # Downgrades (WARN) — worth seeing, but must not fail the baseline yet.
# 90005 — Sec-Fetch-Dest Header is Missing.
# Sec-Fetch-* are REQUEST headers the browser sends; a server cannot set them,
# so there is nothing here to fix. An artifact of the alpha passive rules
# (`-a`), which are kept for their genuine coverage. (#131)

column3: Sec-Fetch-* are request headers the browser sends; not server-controllable

column1: # Downgrades (WARN) — worth seeing, but must not fail the baseline yet.
# 90004 — Insufficient Site Isolation Against Spectre.
# The CONSOLE now sets Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp alongside its
# COOP + CORP, so it is fully cross-origin isolated (ADR-0012, #131). It loads
# no cross-origin subresources — its CSP is `default-src 'self'` — so require-corp
# costs nothing there; verified in a browser (`window.crossOriginIsolated === true`,
# console renders clean).
# The WIDGET deliberately does NOT set it: it is loaded as a subresource *into*
# customer pages, where CORP (`cross-origin`) is the header that matters and
# COEP would constrain the host page rather than protect the widget.
# Kept at WARN so the API — JSON, no browsing context, no COEP — does not fail
# the gate over a header that means nothing there.

column3: Console sets COEP (ADR-0012); widget must stay embeddable; API has no browsing context

column1: # 10063 — Permissions Policy Header Not Set.
# The console sets Permissions-Policy; the API (JSON, no browsing context) does
# not need one. WARN so a genuinely missing header on the console still surfaces.

column3: API responses have no browsing context; console sets Permissions-Policy

column1: # 10049 — Storable and Cacheable Content.
# The console's static assets are deliberately cacheable (`public, immutable`
# for hashed bundles; `no-store` for index.html). Being cacheable is the intent,
# not a defect. WARN keeps it visible without failing.

column3: Hashed static assets are intentionally cacheable; index.html is no-store
